topics.title: Circular orbital velocity
topics.explain: For a stable circular orbit, centripetal acceleration equals gravitational acceleration. Use total mass M of the central body and orbital radius r from its center.
topics.example: Low Earth orbit (~400 km altitude): r ≈ 6.77×10⁶ m, M = M⊕ → v ≈ 7.67 km/s.

topics.title: Escape velocity
topics.explain: Minimum speed to reach infinity from distance r with no further thrust. Exactly √2 times circular orbital speed at the same radius.

topics.title: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation
topics.explain: Relates change in velocity to specific impulse I_sp (seconds), initial mass m₀, and final mass m_f after burning propellant. Foundation of staging and fuel budgets.
topics.example: I_sp = 450 s, mass ratio 10:1 → Δv ≈ 9.8 km/s.

topics.title: Kepler's third law
topics.explain: Orbital period T scales with semi-major axis a; for solar system bodies a in AU and T in years: T² = a³ when M is solar mass.
topics.example: Mars at a ≈ 1.52 AU → T ≈ 1.88 years.

topics.title: Hohmann transfer (approx.)
topics.explain: Most fuel-efficient coplanar transfer between two circular orbits r₁ and r₂ around the same body. Used for interplanetary mission planning.
topics.example: Earth to Mars Hohmann takes ~259 days flight time.

topics.title: Light travel time
topics.explain: Time for light (or radio) to cross distance d. One astronomical unit ≈ 499 s (~8.3 min) from Sun to Earth.

topics.title: Schwarzschild radius
topics.explain: Characteristic radius of a non-rotating black hole. Not a physical surface — defines the event horizon in classical GR.

topics.title: Stefan–Boltzmann luminosity
topics.explain: Power radiated by a blackbody sphere of radius R and effective temperature T. Explains why hot stars are vastly more luminous.

topics.title: Cosmological redshift (concept)
topics.formula: z = Δλ / λ ≈ v / c (low z)
topics.explain: Stretching of wavelength as space expands. High-z galaxies probe early universe; JWST targets z > 10.
topics.example: z = 1 means wavelength doubled; look-back ~7.7 Gyr.

topics.title: Hill sphere (approx.)
topics.explain: Region where a satellite's gravity dominates the tidal pull of a larger body. Moon orbits inside Earth's Hill sphere around the Sun.
topics.example: Earth's Hill sphere extends ~1.5 million km.
